text: Now you, son of man, take a sharp sword and use it as a barber's razor: shave your head and your beard. Then take scales and weigh out the hair, and divide it.

Burn a third of it in the fire inside the city when the days of the siege are ended. Take another third and strike it with the sword all around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind, and I will draw the sword after them.

versions.text: Burn a third of it in the fire inside the city when the days of the siege are完 completed. Take another third and strike it with the sword all around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind, and I will pursue it with the sword.
versions.explanation: A stray non-English character (完) has been left in the text, which would be unreadable when spoken aloud. Also, 'וְחֶרֶב אָרִיק אַחֲרֵיהֶם' more precisely means to unsheathe or draw the sword after them, rather than 'pursue with the sword'.

versions.text: Burn a third of it in the fire inside the city when the days of the siege are ended. Take another third and strike it with the sword all around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind, and I will draw the sword after it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pronoun 'אַחֲרֵיהֶם' is plural, pointing past the hair to the people it symbolizes (as in verse 12). 'After them' is both more accurate and prepares the hearer for the human referent.

text: But take a few strands from it and bind them into the folds of your garment.
And from these take some again, throw them into the fire, and burn them there. From it a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel.

versions.text: And from these take some again, throw them into the fire, and burn them there. Out of it a fire will go out against the whole house of Israel.
versions.explanation: 'Out of it a fire will go out' repeats 'out' awkwardly for oral reading; smoothing the wording improves the rhythm without changing the sense.

text: This is what the Lord GOD says: This is Jerusalem. I set her in the midst of the nations, with countries all around her.
But she rebelled against my judgments more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries around her. They rejected my judgments and did not walk in my statutes.

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations around you, and have not walked in my statutes or kept my judgments—you have not even lived by the standards of the nations around you—
therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: See, I myself am against you, and I will execute judgments in your midst before the eyes of the nations.
Because of all your abominations I will do among you what I have never done before and will never do again.
Therefore fathers will eat their children among you, and children will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments on you and scatter all who remain of you to every wind.

versions.text: Therefore fathers will eat their children among you, and children will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments on you and scatter every survivor of yours to every wind.
versions.explanation: 'Every survivor of yours' is a clumsy possessive for oral reading; 'all who remain of you' renders 'כָּל־שְׁאֵרִיתֵךְ' naturally and flows better when spoken.

text: Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and all your abominations, I myself will cut you down; my eye will not spare, and I will show no pity.

versions.text: Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and all your abominations, I will cut you down; my eye will not spare, and I will show no pity.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew 'וְגַם־אֲנִי' carries emphatic force ('I too / I myself'), matching the following two emphatic clauses. Adding 'myself' preserves the rhetorical weight without lengthening the line.

text: A third of your people will die of plague or waste away from famine within you; a third will fall by the sword around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw the sword after them.

versions.text: A third of your people will die of plague or waste away from famine within you; a third will fall by the sword around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will pursue them with the sword.
versions.explanation: This is the identical Hebrew clause rendered in verse 2 as 'I will draw the sword after them.' The verb 'אָרִיק' means to unsheathe/draw the sword; matching the wording here keeps the deliberate echo between the sign-act and its interpretation.

text: Then my anger will be spent, I will vent my wrath on them and be satisfied. And when I have spent my wrath on them, they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my zeal.
I will make you a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of all who pass by.
You will be an object of scorn and mockery, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I execute judgments on you in anger and wrath and furious rebuke. I, the LORD, have spoken.
When I send the deadly arrows of famine against you—arrows that bring ruin, which I send to destroy you—I will heap famine upon you and cut off your supply of bread.

versions.text: When I send against you the deadly arrows of famine, sent to destroy—when I send them to destroy you—I will intensify the famine against you and cut off your supply of bread.
versions.explanation: The double 'send... when I send' is a stumbling repetition when read aloud; restructuring keeps both Hebrew relative clauses while smoothing the rhythm. 'Heap famine upon you' also reflects 'אֹסֵף עֲלֵיכֶם' (to add or gather more) more closely than 'intensify.'

text: I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will leave you childless. Plague and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken.
